questions.q: How was the scheduled-job semaphore contention fixed, without removing either job?
options: The Nightly Rollup job was moved to run at 2:00 AM, clear of the 7:00 AM submission spike, so the two jobs no longer overlap
Both jobs were deleted entirely
The Morning Reminder job was disabled permanently
The semaphore pool was removed from the instance
questions.explain: Rescheduling one job to a quiet window removes the overlap that caused the semaphore pool to saturate, without losing either job's function.

questions.q: Why is a prevention plan described as the real deliverable of this capstone, not just the three fixes?
options: The three fixes already guarantee no future performance problem can ever occur
A prevention plan replaces the need to diagnose any future issue
Prevention plans are only useful for documentation purposes
Without monitoring, review, and testing in place, the same pattern of inefficiencies invisible at small scale can simply recur as any other app grows
questions.explain: The three causes existed because nobody was watching for the moment growth would expose them -- a prevention plan is what catches the next instance early.

questions.q: Why is an alert tied to usage growth itself more valuable than a response-time alert alone?
options: Usage growth has no real relationship to performance degradation
By the time a response-time metric crosses its threshold, the underlying cause has usually already been accumulating for months
Growth-tied alerts are easier to configure than response-time alerts
Response-time alerts are more accurate than growth-based alerts in every case
questions.explain: A growth-milestone alert can flag risk while a problem is still small, rather than waiting until it has already degraded measurable performance.

questions.q: How does an ATF performance regression test connect to Course 11's Automated Test Framework coverage?
options: It replaces ATF with a completely different testing tool
It only checks that a script's syntax is valid, not its performance
It runs exclusively in production after a deployment, never before
It captures a performance baseline for an app's heaviest operations and fails the build if a future change measurably worsens it
questions.explain: Baselining key operations and failing a build on regression is exactly the guardrail that would have caught the query-in-a-loop before it ever reached production.

questions.q: What is the stated difference in focus between this course and the next course, ServiceNow Technical Architecture?
options: Technical Architecture is a repeat of this course's capstone with a different company name
This course fixes performance problems after they appear; Technical Architecture focuses on design decisions made before such problems can exist
This course and Technical Architecture cover identical material in a different order
Technical Architecture has nothing to do with performance at all
questions.explain: The closing reflection frames the shift explicitly: from diagnosing and fixing after the fact to designing with scale in mind from day one.
